description: This Java source file defines the ShoppingListServices class, providing static methods for managing shopping lists within the OFBiz framework. The functions include creating recurrences, cloning order items into shopping lists, updating quantities from orders, auto-deleting saved shopping lists, and converting shopping lists into shopping carts. It appears to be part of the order shopping list component of the OFBiz e-commerce system, supporting complex shopping list management and automation.

classes.name: ShoppingListServices
classes.description: Provides static service methods for managing shopping lists, including scheduling recurrences, creating reorders, updating list quantities from orders, handling list and cart conversions, and automated cleanup of saved lists.

methods.name: setShoppingListRecurrence
methods.description: Creates recurrence info for shopping list based on provided start/end dates, frequency, and interval, returning the recurrence ID to schedule repeated shopping list actions.

methods.name: createListReorders
methods.description: Automates reordering of shopping lists that are active and due for reorder based on their recurrence info, creating new orders and updating last ordered date.

methods.name: splitShipmentMethodString
methods.description: Parses a combined shipment method string into shipment method type ID and carrier party ID.

methods.name: makeListFromOrder
methods.description: Generates a shopping list from an existing order, optionally creating a new list, and copying order items into the list.

methods.name: makeShoppingListCart
methods.description: Creates a new ShoppingCart object based on a shopping list, or adds shopping list items to an existing cart.

methods.name: updateShoppingListQuantitiesFromOrder
methods.description: Updates quantities purchased in shopping list items based on an existing order, aiding in tracking purchases.

methods.name: autoDeleteAutoSaveShoppingList
methods.description: Automatically deletes old or completed auto-save shopping lists, with paging, transactions, and cleanup logic.
